text: Latvia Moves to Expel Russian Journalist Leonid Ragozin, Delfi Reports Oct. 7, 2026 Leonid Ragozin. Facebook Latvian authorities have launched proceedings to declare Riga-based Russian journalist Leonid Ragozin persona non grata, Delfi reported Tuesday. While Ragozin was not identified by name, Foreign Minister Baiba Braže announced blacklisting proceedings against a Russian citizen based on new information from “competent authorities” and discussions with the prime minister. Sources familiar with the matter told Delfi that the move targets Ragozin, who has resided in Latvia since around the time of Russia’s annexation of Crimea in 2014. There was no indication when the decision would be made. Ragozin drew public ire for comments he made on a podcast hosted by Aaron Maté of fringe far-left outlet The Grayzone, which has been accused of taking a pro-Russian slant. He argued that Russia was compelled to respond to the West with “brute force,” saying, “ [Russia] always consider themselves as the underdogs and as the side that is being under constant pressure from the West, encroaching on its sphere of influence, on its strategic interests. title: Russian Who Swam to Lithuania to Seek Asylum Gets 6 Years in Russian Prison After Return
text: Russian Who Swam to Lithuania to Seek Asylum Gets 6 Years in Russian Prison After Return Oct. 7, 2026 The Lithuanian side of the border with Russia. Lithuanian MOD A Russian man who swam across the Neman River to Lithuania seeking asylum was sentenced to six years in prison after Lithuanian authorities returned him to Russia, media reported. The Baltic Fleet Military Court on Sept. 30 found Igor Odintsov guilty of publicly calling for terrorism, the regional news outlet Russky Zapad reported . He will serve his sentence in a high-security penal colony. The court found that Odintsov had posted messages on a messaging app that portrayed the “ideology and practice of terrorism as correct and deserving of support and emulation.” Investigators also said he held “radical views,” opposed Russia’s invasion of Ukraine and had a “negative attitude” toward the Russian authorities. The Lithuanian news outlet Lrytas identified Odintsov, 68, as the Kaliningrad region resident who swam across the Neman on Sept. 17 and sought asylum, saying he faced persecution in Russia over his social media posts. news ‘It Still Causes Severe Stress’: Fear of Expulsion Upends Life for Some Russian Asylum Seekers

title: Rosatom Takes Full Control of Transport Conglomerate Delo Group in $900M Buyout
text: Rosatom Takes Full Control of Transport Conglomerate Delo Group in $900M Buyout Oct. 7, 2026 Sergei Shishkarev, founder of Delo. Semenforyou (CC BY-SA 4.0) Russian state nuclear corporation Rosatom has completed its acquisition of founder Sergei Shishkarev’s remaining 51% stake in transport conglomerate Delo, both parties announced Wednesday. Neither party disclosed the amount Rosatom paid, though Shishkarev has valued his stake in Delo at 77 billion rubles ($900.3 million). “From this moment, we begin the final consolidation of all Rosatom logistics assets, which will result in the creation of the largest national logistics company,” Rosatom CEO Alexei Likhachev said in a statement. Likhachev said the deal brought Rosatom’s market share in Russia’s container handling market to 50% and rail container transport to 44%. He boasted that Rosatom’s logistics arm operates in all Russian maritime basins, owns the country’s largest container fleet and owns port facilities in major cities. On Tuesday, French President Emmanuel Macron hailed the test of the submarine-launched ballistic missile off the coast of Brittany as a message "sent loud and clear for wherever it must be received," without mentioning Russia directly. The launch came amid heightened tensions over the war in Ukraine, European security and nuclear deterrence. title: Northern Russia’s Yamalo-Nenets Offers 1M-Ruble Bounty for Downed Drones
text: Northern Russia’s Yamalo-Nenets Offers 1M-Ruble Bounty for Downed Drones Oct. 7, 2026 Yulia Morozova / Moskva News Agency Authorities in northwestern Russia’s Yamalo-Nenets autonomous district have established a reward of 1 million rubles ($11,700) for reservists who successfully shoot down enemy drones. It is the highest publicly recorded bounty offered by any Russian region for downing Ukrainian drones, according to the state-run news agency TASS. Other regions offer significantly lower rewards, ranging from 20,000 rubles to 200,000 rubles. Reservists operating in Yamal’s mobile firing squads will qualify for an equal share of the bounty if the intercepted drone does not cause damage to local infrastructure, according to a regional decree cited by the agency. Previously, a one-time reward of 1 million rubles was reportedly awarded to a serviceman in the republic of Chechnya last December. Located around 2,200 kilometers (1,367 miles) from the Ukrainian border, the natural gas-rich Yamalo-Nenets was struck by Ukrainian drones for the first time in early September. title: Second Prison Guard Dead After Failed Inmate Escape Attempt in North Caucasus
text: Second Prison Guard Dead After Failed Inmate Escape Attempt in North Caucasus Oct. 7, 2026 The Russian Investigative Committee A Russian prisoner who was extradited from Georgia last month was shot dead after attempting to escape a transport train in the North Caucasus last week, killing two prison guards and injuring two others. The Federal Penitentiary Service (FSIN) on Wednesday confirmed the second officer died in a hospital from wounds sustained last Friday, Oct. 2, during the incident at a station in the republic of Kabardino-Balkaria. One guard died at the scene near the Murtazovo station en route from the republic of North Ossetia-Alania to the Krasnodar region. FSIN said it shot and killed the inmate on the spot. The surviving officers who contained the situation will receive state honors, while the families of the two deceased guards will receive financial support, FSIN said. The deceased inmate was reportedly identified as 43-year-old Dmitry Pushkaryov, who was extradited from Georgia to Russia on Sept. 24 alongside another suspect. text: U.S. Embassy Urges Citizens to Leave Russia Over Siberian Plague Suspicions Oct. 7, 2026 A car drives past a sign in Shelekhov in Russia's Irkutsk region. REUTERS / Stringer The U.S. Embassy in Moscow issued a health alert on Tuesday over the death of a plague lab worker in the Irkutsk region, urging Americans to leave Russia and those in the affected area to follow local health guidance. The death of an Irkutsk anti-plague institute employee last week has fueled fears of a possible outbreak, though authorities have not publicly confirmed that she had the disease. U.S. State Secretary Marco Rubio urged Russia to share more information, while President Donald Trump said he planned to address the matter in a call with President Vladimir Putin. “U.S. citizens in the area should follow the guidance of local health authorities, avoid affected facilities, and seek medical care promptly if they develop fever or respiratory symptoms,” the U.S. Embassy in Moscow said in a statement. text: Kim Jong Un Wishes Putin ‘Victory and Glory’ on His 74th Birthday Oct. 7, 2026 Vladimir Putin and Kim Jong Un. kremlin.ru North Korean leader Kim Jong Un wished President Vladimir Putin “victory and glory” on his 74th birthday Wednesday, pledging to deepen ties as Pyongyang continues to support Russia’s war in Ukraine. “My dearest friend, Comrade Vladimir Putin, please accept my most heartfelt and warm congratulations and best wishes on the occasion of your birthday,” Kim wrote in a telegram published by North Korea’s state-run Korean Central News Agency. Kim praised Putin’s “outstanding and skillful leadership,” saying Russia had strengthened its standing as a world power over the past two decades. text: Sochi Closes Beaches After Drone Attack Sets Oil Tanker Ablaze Oct. 7, 2026 Social media / Reuters Authorities in Russia’s Black Sea resort city of Sochi and the neighboring federal territory of Sirius closed beaches after a tanker caught fire offshore following a reported attack by naval drones, officials said Tuesday. Sochi Mayor Andrei Proshunin said the city’s beaches and waterfront promenades would remain closed until further notice. The decision followed a meeting with security officials, emergency responders and public health and weather agencies. “I ask residents and visitors to Sochi not to put themselves at risk and to wait for an official decision on reopening,” Proshunin wrote on Telegram. Sirius officials also closed all beaches and urged residents to limit their time outdoors and keep windows shut where possible. “We are continuously monitoring water and air quality together with Roshydromet,” Sirius administration head Dmitry Plishkin said , referring to Russia’s weather and environmental monitoring agency. title: Russia Drops Criminal Case Against Children’s Hospice Founder Lida Moniava
text: Russia Drops Criminal Case Against Children’s Hospice Founder Lida Moniava Oct. 7, 2026 Lida Moniava. REUTERS / Anastasia Barashkova Russian investigators have dropped a criminal case against Lida Moniava, a prominent advocate for critically ill children’s care, after finding no grounds for prosecution, her supporters said Tuesday, citing her lawyer. Moniava was arrested on Sept. 2 and charged with spreading “false information” about Russia’s military over a social media post about Ukrainian civilians killed in Russian attacks. The charge carries a maximum sentence of 10 years in prison. Her support group said lawyer Mikhail Biryukov had confirmed the decision and that an official notice closing the case had been sent by mail. “This is a miracle. But it didn’t happen on its own. You made it happen,” the group wrote, thanking those who attended her court hearing, wrote letters in her defense and publicly supported her. text: At Least 24 Killed in Ukraine, Zelensky Condemns One of Russia's Most 'Vile Strikes' By Reuters Oct. 7, 2026 Rescuers work at a site of an apartment building damaged by a Russian missile strike, amid Russia's attack on Ukraine, in the town of Pryluky, Chernihiv region. Ukrainian State Emergency Service Russia pounded Ukraine with waves of missiles and drones in one of its most "vile strikes" on Wednesday, President Volodymyr Zelensky said, killing at least 24 people, including children, and damaging industrial facilities and energy infrastructure. The heaviest death toll was in Pryluky in Ukraine's northern Chernihiv region, where a Russian missile obliterated a five-story residential building. At least 18 people, including four children, were killed there, local officials said. Zelensky said the strike coincided with Russian President Vladimir Putin's birthday. "Today, as a birthday 'gift' to Putin, the Russian army destroyed a residential building in Pryluky," Zelensky said, adding that six more people were also killed in Kyiv, Oleksandria and Kremenchuk during the massive attack.
